definitions.explanation: A person, typically a child, who cries frequently or easily. Can be used teasingly or descriptively.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}はなきむしだ。
{小|ちい}さい{頃|ころ}はなきむしだったけど、{今|いま}は{強|つよ}くなった。
examples.english: I was a crybaby when I was little, but now I've become strong.

notes:
なきむし describes a person (usually a child) who cries frequently or easily. Can also be written in kanji as {泣|な}き{虫|むし}.

WORD FORMATION:
{泣|な}き (crying, from {泣|な}く) + {虫|むし} (bug). The むし suffix creates personality-type words implying the person is "infested" with the trait.

THE ～{虫|むし} PATTERN:
- なきむし/{泣|な}き{虫|むし}: crybaby
- {弱虫|よわむし}: coward, weakling
- {怠|なま}け{虫|むし}: lazybones
- {泣|な}き{虫|むし}: crybaby (same as なきむし)

USAGE:
Most commonly used among children as a mild taunt. Adults may use it self-deprecatingly ({子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}はなきむしだった — I was a crybaby as a kid). Not strongly offensive but can sting depending on context.

RELATED PERSONALITY WORDS:
- {甘|あま}えん{坊|ぼう}: clingy/spoiled person
- {意気地|いくじ}なし: coward, gutless person
- {照|て}れ{屋|や}: easily embarrassed person
